definition.label: a cellar room
definition.notice: CELLAR ROOM TO LET. Dry enough. A straw bed and a crate.
definition.night: You sleep on the straw in your cellar, your own door bolted. Damp, but nobody snores but you.

definition.label: a garret room
definition.notice: GARRET TO LET under the roof. A plank bed. Light from the dormer window.
definition.night: You sleep in your garret under the tiles. The wind walks on the roof, but the door is yours.

definition.label: a room at a widow's
definition.notice: A CLEAN ROOM TO LET to a quiet single man. Bed and linen. Coffee in the morning. Ask the widow.
definition.night: You sleep between the widow's linen sheets. In the morning there is coffee and a heel of bread.

definition.label: a small house in an alley
definition.notice: HOUSE TO LET in the alley. One room down, a box bed, its own hearth.
definition.night: You sleep in the box bed of your own house, the hearth's last embers ticking. The alley is quiet.

definition.label: a merchant's upper floor
definition.notice: FIRST FLOOR TO LET over the counting house. Two tall windows on the river, a marble fireplace, a bed in an alcove, furnished.
definition.night: You sleep in the alcove bed on the first floor, the fire ticking as it dies. Ships' lights move on the ceiling.

looks.label: read the notice board
looks.text: The notice board by the door: a proclamation of the College of Burgomaster and Aldermen about dogs without muzzles, and the militia lists. Nothing new pasted up today.

looks.label: look at the register on the counter
looks.text: The register of the civil state lies open on the counter: births, deaths and marriages in a clerk's copperplate. Nothing written in it yet today.

looks.label: look up the staircase
looks.text: The old courtyard of the town hall, roofed over with glass, and a great stair of white stone going up to the fine floor. Floris's arcades carry the galleries round it.

looks.label: look at the chimneypiece
looks.text: The chimneypiece of the wedding hall: two women carved in alabaster carry the mantel on their heads, three hundred years old and scorched by the fire of the Spanish Fury. A fire burns under them.

looks.label: look at the paintings
looks.text: The Leys hall: Hendrik Leys painted the town's old privileges and its burghers on these walls, finished only three years ago. Dark, stiff, splendid figures in black and red.

looks.label: look out at the square
looks.text: The Grote Markt through small leaded panes: the guild houses, the stalls, a dray at the well. The glass is old and bends the gables a little.

looks.label: look at the barrels
looks.text: Barrels of wine in racks two high, stencilled with the names of Bordeaux houses and Rhine towns. The old meat hall smells of oak and must now, not of blood.

looks.label: look up at the vaults
looks.text: Brick vaults on stone columns, three aisles of them, built for the butchers' guild in 1504. Soot from lanterns streaks the brick.

looks.label: look at the tasting table
looks.text: A table among the casks: two bottles, three glasses with a red rim of wine, a candle stuck in its own wax, the cellar book open at a page of figures. Here the buyers taste before they bargain.

looks.label: read the chalk on the casks
looks.text: Chalk on the cask heads, in the cellar master's hand: a cross, a year, the first letters of a Bordeaux house, a buyer's name half rubbed out.

looks.label: look at the bottle racks
looks.text: Pigeonholes of dark bottles, necks in, dust on every one. The better growths lie down here till they are sold.

looks.label: look at the hoist
looks.text: A jib on a post over the skids by the north door, a pulley block and a rope. A cask swings slowly on it, going up to be rolled out or coming down to be laid on the stillage.

looks.label: look at the stage
looks.text: A small stage with a painted castle and town on the backcloth, red curtains looped back, a row of candle footlights. The society Liefde en Eendragt plays here.

looks.label: look at the canvases
looks.text: A studio: canvases turned to the wall, one on each easel half done, a model's platform with a draped chair. The light falls in a grey sheet from the gable's windows.

looks.label: look into the cases
looks.text: Under the glass: Roman pots and coins dug out of the old Burcht and the river mud, green bronze pins, a clay lamp, a medieval jug, wax seals of the guilds, a fossil shell as big as a hand. Each has a small card in careful French and Flemish.

looks.label: look into the cabinet
looks.text: A tall cabinet: small carved saints from demolished churches, a bronze mortar, a pewter jug with the town's arms.

looks.label: look at the old stones
looks.text: Carved stones along the wall: a tombstone with a knight worn almost smooth, the capital of a column from a church that is gone, a Roman altar stone, the arms of the town cut in stone.

looks.label: look at the armour
looks.text: A suit of armour on a stand, empty and patient, and racks of halberds and pikes of the town's old militia. For looking at only: the attendant watches your hands.

looks.label: look at the bronze gun
looks.text: A small bronze gun on a wooden carriage, green with age, the maker's name and a date cast on the barrel.

looks.label: look down the stair
looks.text: A worn stair goes down into the dark: the old prison cells under the castle. The last stop of the museum.

looks.label: look round the cell
looks.text: The old prison of the Steen. Until fifty years ago men waited here for the judges: a low stone ceiling, iron rings in the wall, a bench, straw on the floor. Names and crosses are scratched into the stone.

looks.label: look at the stacks
looks.text: Sacks of coffee and grain in pyramids, bales of wool and cotton corded tight, crates and casks, each marked in chalk with a number from the storekeeper's book. It smells of jute, tar and old timber.

looks.label: look at the scale
looks.text: A decimal scale on the floor: a sack goes on the platform, the storekeeper slides a weight along the beam and writes the figure down.

looks.label: look round the hall
looks.text: The house of the Hanse's merchants, three hundred years old: once their counting rooms and chambers, now a warehouse of the Belgian State. Forty windows, a great tower over the gate, and in here only dust and goods.

looks.label: look up at the hoist
looks.text: A rope comes down through a hatch in the ceiling with a hook on it: goods go up and down between the floors on it.

looks.label: look at the court gate
looks.text: The gate to the court is barred. Through the cracks: cobbles, a pump, the wings round it, rows of windows over dusty lofts.

looks.label: look at the Elevation of the Cross
looks.text: Rubens's Elevation of the Cross, the great triptych, back in Antwerp since the French gave it up in 1815. Men strain with ropes and shoulders to heave the cross upright on a slant; on the wings the mourners grieve and the Roman officer gives his orders from the saddle.

looks.label: look at the Descent from the Cross
looks.text: Rubens's Descent from the Cross. A pale body slides down a white sheet into many hands; a young man in a red cloak takes its weight. On the wings the Visitation and the Presentation in the Temple. The arquebusiers' guild paid for it, two hundred and sixty years ago.

looks.label: look at the high altar
looks.text: Over the high altar, in black and white marble and gold, Our Lady rises on clouds among the angels while the apostles stare into her empty tomb: Rubens again, his Assumption. The altar is new, fifty years old, built from the marble of a church the French pulled down. The red lamp before the tabernacle never goes out.

looks.label: look at the Resurrection
looks.text: A smaller triptych in a chapel off the ambulatory: Christ bursts from the tomb with a red banner and the guards fall back from the light. A printer's widow had it painted for her husband's grave.

looks.label: look up into the dome
looks.text: High over the crossing the lantern opens to a painted dome: rings of clouds and angels climbing toward the light, and Our Lady rising at the top. Painted two hundred years ago; from down here it swims in the dusk and the daylight of the lantern's windows.

looks.label: look at the pulpit
looks.text: The pulpit is carved oak, all of it: at its foot four women for Europe, Asia, Africa and America with a horse, a camel, a lion and a crocodile; trees rise from them, their branches full of birds, an eagle and a peacock among them; angels blow trumpets on the sounding board. It came from the abbey at Hemiksem when the French closed it.

looks.label: look at the choir stalls
looks.text: Behind the rail the canons' stalls run down both sides of the choir in new pale oak: pointed arches, gables and pinnacles, carved these thirty years and still not finished. The old stalls went to the fire in the French years.

looks.label: look up at the organ
looks.text: Up on the west gallery over the door the organ's carved case climbs toward the great west window: towers of tin pipes, gilt crests, angels with trumpets on top.

looks.label: look at the font
looks.text: The font by the door, black marble with a white bowl under an oak cover. A drop of holy water on your fingers is cold as the Schelde.

looks.label: read a grave slab
looks.text: A worn slab in the floor: a merchant, his wife, a coat of arms and a skull, and a date two hundred years gone. Ten thousand boots have walked his name smooth.

table.name: a deal table
table.note: Scrubbed pine, rings from other men's pots.

rug.name: a rag rug
rug.note: Woven from old coats. Keeps the cold off the floor.

stove.name: a cast-iron stove
stove.note: A little pot-bellied stove, pipe included. Heavy.

plant.name: a geranium in a pot
plant.note: Red, a bit leggy. Wants the light.

birdcage.name: a finch in a cage
birdcage.note: A chaffinch in a wicker cage on a stand. It sings at dawn.

picture.name: a framed print
picture.note: The cathedral spire in a black frame. Hang it on a wall.

lamp.name: a hanging oil lamp
lamp.note: Brass font, glass chimney. Hang it from a beam.

clock.name: a wall clock
clock.note: A Black Forest clock. It ticks; the hour is the town's.

curtains.name: a pair of curtains
curtains.note: Faded red wool. For a window.
